title: EFFECTIVE HANDS
mv: He who has a slack hand becomes poor, But the hand of the diligent makes rich.
mvp: ‘‘He who has a slack hand becomes poor, But the hand of the diligent makes rich.’’ Proverbs 10:4 (NKJV)
assignment: List five (5) ways your hands have been effective for God in the past month (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: The human hand is made up of 27 bones, including carpal bones (wrist), metacarpals (palm), and phalanges (finger bones), and it can perform complex actions. Hand movements serve as a powerful tool for expressing thoughts and ideas. Effective hands have to do with making necessary progress toward set goals in relation to creative expressions and physical labour. Human hands are tools, and the hand-work relationship is key to human growth and development. Working with our hands improves memories, stimulates different parts of the brain, reduces stress and boosts executive functions.

The human brain controls hand movements and shapes their use. It also uses the hands to manipulate objects and foster creativity through a process called ‘embodied cognition. ’It is therefore important to always engage our minds positively to put our hands to work. Man is a creative being because we possess the creative ability of God (Exodus 35:30-33). We must therefore occupy our thoughts positively so that our hands can be continually creative since the brain controls ‘‘high order’’ such as thoughts, reasoning and abstraction. Remember, you are the product of your thoughts (Proverbs 23:7). We need to stimulate our thoughts’ creative ability and move on to engage our hands (Ecclesiastes 9:10) to be at work to produce the innovative ideas that come to our minds. We must think through ground-breaking ideas that will bring about solutions to problems around us.

These are hands put into effective use to prevent physical, spiritual, innovative, emotional and financial poverty. These hands do not give room for idleness (Proverbs 31:27; Ecclesiastes 10:18). They are put to diligent use; as a result, the owners of such hands dominate anywhere they find themselves (Proverbs 12:24). People with strong and diligent hands are known for diversity as their creative minds birth various ideas that their hands explore (Proverbs 31:13-16). There is no room for sloppiness and slothfulness of these hands (Proverbs 24:30-31; 19:24). These hands are always involved in learning, teaching, empowerment and creativity through brilliant ideas from the mind (Luke 19:13). Strong hands are also known for hard work which results in riches, blessings and abundance (Acts 20:34; 1 Corinthians 4:12a). They may be involved in volunteering by using their chosen field to help the needy, support the weak and offer help to the helpless. These hands serve God, touch lives positively through their creative prowess and do exploits.
It is counterproductive not to use the hands for productive purposes, as this can lead to a decline in hand function, loss of strength and dexterity over time.
Put your hands to effective use and be a blessing to yourself and humanity.
